$comment: The one source of release notes: the in-app What's New sheet, the release tag and the App Store "What's New" all read this. Newest first. One entry per marketing version in app.config.js. Rules (whats-new.test.ts enforces most of them): no league, club, player or brand names; no real people, politics or tragedy; family-friendly; every claim true of the build that ships it. See CLAUDE.md. A callout may carry "to" (a key of CALLOUT_DESTINATIONS in features/whats-new/notes.ts: play, games, leaderboard, challenges, stats, account): tapping it closes the sheet and opens that tab. Leave it out when the feature has no place of its own. To force the sheet without recording anything: ?whatsnew=<version> on the web, or in a development build on iOS the launch argument -whatsnew <version|current>, e.g. `xcrun simctl launch booted com.eighteenzerodcai.app -whatsnew current`.

versions.headline: We were on a bye.
versions.subhead: The trade deadline just slammed shut, the playoff race is on, and the holiday games are close. Here is what is new on the field.

callouts.title: Seventeen and oh
callouts.line: A season is 17 games now. Perfect means 17-0.

callouts.title: Fresh turf
callouts.line: Navy stands and field-green grass, from icon to share card.

callouts.title: Brag, properly
callouts.line: Shares lead with your record, and the result card rides along.

callouts.title: Flag on the play
callouts.line: Every name on the leaderboards can be reported now.

notes: Seasons are 17 games long, so the perfect season is 17-0. Ratings did not move: the same seven cards earn the same rating as before, and only the record it maps to changed.
The game opens in Turf: navy stands and field-green grass, with the same look on the icon, the splash screen and the share card.
A share leads with your record and ends with a link to the game, and the result card goes with it wherever the share sheet takes an image.
Every name on the leaderboards carries a report flag, not only the rows in the plain list.
On the web, the ranked switch tells screen readers whether it is on, and banners hold their space while they load so the roster no longer jumps.
